goals: Classify decomposition reactions as thermal, electrolytic, or photolytic
Recognise displacement, double displacement, and precipitation reactions

cards.title: Combination Reaction
cards.body:
In a combination reaction, two or more reactants join to form a single product.

For example, calcium oxide reacts with water to form calcium hydroxide: CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂.

cards.title: Decomposition Reaction
cards.body:
A decomposition reaction is the opposite. One reactant breaks into two or more simpler products.

Thermal decomposition uses heat. Electrolytic decomposition uses electricity. Photolytic decomposition uses light.

cards.title: Types of Decomposition
cards.remember: Decomposition reactions need an external energy source to break the bonds.

rows.value: Requires heat, like CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂

cards.question: Which reaction is a photolytic decomposition?
cards.why: Photolytic decomposition is caused by light. Silver chloride breaks down into silver and chlorine when exposed to sunlight. The other options are thermal and electrolytic decompositions and a displacement reaction.

cards.title: Displacement and Double Displacement Reactions
cards.body:
In a displacement reaction, a more reactive element replaces a less reactive element in a compound.

In a double displacement reaction, the ions of two compounds exchange places. If a solid forms, it is a precipitation reaction.

steps: A student mixes aqueous solutions of lead nitrate and potassium iodide.
The balanced equation is Pb(NO₃)₂ + 2KI → PbI₂ + 2KNO₃.
Lead iodide is a yellow solid that precipitates out of the solution.
This is a double displacement reaction because the ions exchange partners, and it is also a precipitation reaction because a solid forms.
cards.question: What happens when aqueous lead nitrate and potassium iodide are mixed?
What type of reaction is Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu?
cards.why: Zinc displaces copper from copper sulphate because zinc is more reactive than copper. This is a single displacement reaction.

cards.title: Exothermic and Endothermic Reactions
cards.body:
An exothermic reaction releases heat into the surroundings.

An endothermic reaction absorbs heat from the surroundings to proceed, making the surroundings feel cold.

cards.question: Which reaction is endothermic?
cards.why: Endothermic reactions absorb heat. Calcium carbonate breaks down only while it keeps absorbing heat, so its decomposition is endothermic. Rusting, burning coal and neutralisation all release heat, so they are exothermic.

points: Combination reactions form one product from two or more reactants.
Decomposition reactions break one reactant into two or more products using heat, electricity, or light.
Displacement reactions involve a more reactive element replacing a less reactive one.
Double displacement reactions involve ion exchange and often result in a precipitate.
Exothermic reactions release heat, while endothermic reactions absorb heat.
